item.title: 269220 : I-71 North-South between MM 0.1 and 2.0 Between I-64/I-71 Interchange and Zorn Ave. in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The I-71 widening and improvement project is a $50 million infrastructure investment to enhance safety and improve mobility along one of Louisville's most critical travel corridors. The two-year project, focused on increasing traffic capacity and safety, will enhance regional connectivity, provide reliable travel for years to come, and support economic growth. The project spans approximately two miles of interstate from the I-65/I-71 interchange near Frankfort Avenue to the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange. Additional improvements include the construction of a multi-use path along Zorn Avenue between the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange and Mellwood Avenue, as well as a new median treatment at the intersection of Zorn Avenue and Mellwood Avenue to enhance safety and better define traffic movements. The project also includes the demolition and reconstruction of the I-71 bridge over Beargrass Creek, along with a latex overlay on the I-71 bridge over I-64 at mile point 0.3 to extend the structure’s service life. For additional information, please visit https://transportation.ky.gov/DistrictFive/Pages/I-71-Widening---Louisville-.aspx.

item.title: 292980 : I-71/75 North Ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Boulevard in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : (June 5, 2026) – Interstate 71/75 ramp closures and detours in Covington are needed to safely advance construction on the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, which will add interstate lanes, better access, a new companion bridge and convert the existing bridge for local travel to improve safety and increase regional highway capacity. Temporary closures and detours will now begin on Monday, June 8, and will take place in multiple phases. On Monday, June 8, the following closures are expected to take place: I-71/75 northbound off-ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Blvd. (0.0 - 0.28 mile points): this closure will remain in place through Summer 2027. Detour: Traffic will use the I-71/75 northbound 5th Street exit ramp, turn left (north) onto Philadelphia Street, then left onto 4th Street driving west to the I-71/75 southbound ramp to Pike Street. Turn left on to Pike Street, then right on to Simon Kenton Way, then left on to MLK Blvd. KYTC will provide further updates ahead of the closures to inform all road users via the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project website. [links-1.govdelivery.com] Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. item.title: 310577 : I-71/75 North-South between MM 188.5 and 191.7 Between Kyles Lane and Brent Spence Bridge in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (Nov. 5, 2026) -- The traffic impacts for Wednesday, Nov. 5 as part of the ongoing electrical project for the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project have been adjusted. Work tonight (Thursday, Nov. 5), will include a double left lane closure on Interstates 71/75 northbound in the project area. A single left lane closure will take place at 8 p.m. This will shift to a double left lane closure beginning at 11 p.m. A single right lane closure on I-71/75 southbound will be in place beginning at 8 p.m. All lanes reopen by 5 a.m. on Friday, Nov. 6. Work is expected to continue with single left lane closure in both directions overnight as the project progresses. KYTC will provide updates if additional traffic impacts are required to complete the project. This electrical work is expected to be completed by Monday, Nov. 30. COVINGTON, Ky. (Sept. 25, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of nightly lane closures on Interstates 71/75 in Kenton County beginning Monday, Sept. 28. Crews will be performing electrical work as part of the ongoing Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project. This work will require a nightly northbound and southbound left lane closure from Kyles Lane (KY 1072) (188.52 mile point) to the Brent Spence Bridge (191.63 mile point), a distance of 3.11 miles. Both left lanes (northbound and southbound) will be blocked from 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. All lanes will reopen by 5 a.m. No lane closures associated with this portion of the project will be in place from Thursday, Oct. 8 through Sunday, Oct. 11 due to BLINK. Weather permitting, this portion of the project is expected to be completed Friday, Oct. 23. Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. About the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project The Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project is one of the nation’s most significant transportation transformations, spanning eight miles of I-71/75 in Kentucky and I-75 in Ohio. Construction will begin with the new companion bridge to the west of the Brent Spence Bridge and one mile of approach work in each state. In addition to the new bridge, the project will restripe the existing Brent Spence Bridge to carry local traffic; improve safety and reduce congestion by separating local and through travel; redesign ramp configurations throughout the corridor; and add new pedestrian and bicycle connections linking neighborhoods to jobs and transit. This once-in-a-generation investment will strengthen national freight movement, support local businesses and workforce growth, and enhance quality of life for the millions who rely on this critical corridor. The project team coordinates with all navigation apps so drivers can easily determine the best route from their starting point to their destination. For more information, visit brentspencebridgecorridor.com.

item.description: Construction / Road Work : A road rehabilitation project between Sparta Pike (KY 35) and northeast of the Boone Road (KY 465) overpass is in progress. item.description: Construction / Road Work : Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of daily blasting operations on Interstate 64 West beginning Wednesday, Sept. 2. item.title: 304488 : I-471 North-South between MM 3.7 and 5.0 Area of Daniel Carter Beard Bridge in Campbell County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (Nov. 6, 2026): As the bridge painting and cleaning project on the Memorial Parkway bridge overpass over I-471 nears completion, crews will be shifting to milling and paving operations on I-471 beginning Monday, Nov. 9. On both I-471 northbound and southbound, motorists should expect a single lane closure in the project area at 8 p.m. and a double lane closure at 10 p.m. All lanes are expected to reopen daily by 6 a.m. Weather permitting, milling and paving operations are expected to be completed Wednesday, Nov. 11 at 6 a.m. Permanent striping and rumble strip installation will follow at a later date. KYTC will provide updates once the final portions of work are scheduled. COVINGTON, Ky. (Sept. 3, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of a bridge painting and cleaning project on the Memorial Parkway (KY 1120) bridge overpass over Interstate 471 in Campbell County. This project is expected to begin on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Beginning Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 8 p.m., crews will start the process for a traffic shift on I-471 southbound from south of the Dave Cowens Drive (KY 8X) exit (Exit 5) to south of Memorial Parkway (3.7 mile point), a distance of 1.3 miles. Once completed, traffic will shift to the right toward the outside wall. Access to the Memorial Parkway on/off ramps to and from I-471 will be maintained. On I-471 northbound, contractors will block the left and right shoulders from south of the Memorial Parkway overpass (3.7 mile point) to a railroad bridge (4.0 mile marker) to perform cleaning and painting operations. Three lanes of I-471 southbound and northbound will be maintained during daytime hours. As the project progresses, various single and double lane closures may take place during evening/overnight hours. These lane closures will take place overnight to mitigate travel delays. KYTC will advise ahead of when these closures will take place. The project team will monitor the construction schedule and coordinate to minimize travel delays during major weekend events like BLINK. All lanes and the sidewalk on the Memorial Parkway overpass are expected to remain open throughout much of the project. As the project progresses, a single lane and sidewalk closure will be in place to allow crews a safe area to replace joint seals on each end of the bridge. KYTC will advise ahead of when these closures are expected to take place. This project will address necessary repairs following a crash and subsequent fire on I-471 southbound in March 2026. The project will remove soot damage, clean the bridge and repaint the structure to protect it for years to come. Additionally, I-471 southbound will be resurfaced north of the overpass, and the concrete median will be repaired. Euro Paint LLC is contracted to perform the $1,758,697 project on behalf of KYTC. Weather permitting, the overall project has an expected completion date of Nov. 15, 2026.

item.title: 312041 : I-64 East at MM 36.0 East of KY 53 in Shelby County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : LOUISVILLE, Ky. (Nov. 4, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of upcoming lane closures on Interstate 64 beginning Friday, Nov. 6, as part of the $118 million widening and improvement project of I-64 in Shelby County [links-1.govdelivery.com]. One lane of I-64 East and West from Exit 28 (KY 1848 – Simpsonville) to Exit 32 (KY 55 – Shelbyville/Taylorsville) will be closed starting Friday, Nov. 6, to Thursday, Nov. 12, for rumble strip and permanent striping installation. Work will begin with a left-lane closure; once the rumble strip and striping installations are complete, the closure will shift to the right lane for the same operations. The lane closure will remain in place until the work is complete. Additionally, alternating lane closures will occur nightly on I-64 East at mile marker 36 (east of KY 53) from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. from Sunday, Nov. 8, to Friday, Nov. 13. The alternating lane closures are necessary for contract crews to perform milling and paving operations in preparation for an upcoming traffic shift of I-64. Motorists should heed signage and use caution when traveling through the work zones. All work being performed is part of the $118 million I-64 widening and improvement project in Shelby County, which began in February 2025. The project will increase capacity, upgrade a key interchange, and modernize bridges, ensuring a more efficient and reliable transportation network for motorists. The interstate project is expected to be completed by the Fall of 2027. More details, including project timelines [links-1.govdelivery.com] and traffic impacts [links-1.govdelivery.com], will be shared online as work progresses. Motorists are encouraged to sign up for email alerts [links-1.govdelivery.com] regarding weekly traffic impacts pertaining to the project. The date and duration of this work may be adjusted if inclement weather or other unforeseen delays occur. For the latest traffic and travel updates across the Commonwealth of Kentucky, visit goky.ky.gov [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Information specific to District 5 counties is also available on Facebook [links-1.govdelivery.com] and X [links-1.govdelivery.com].

item.title: 254857 : I-264 East-West between MM 21.5 and 22.9 Area of US-42 in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (March 23, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of overnight lane and ramp closures on Interstate 264 East and West (Watterson Expressway) beginning Tuesday, March 24, as part of the $130 million widening and improvement project of I-264 and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Beginning Tuesday, March 24, at 8 p.m., through Wednesday, March 25, at 6 a.m.: Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East and West between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Beginning Wednesday, March 25, at 8 p.m., through Thursday, March 26, at 6 a.m.: The I-264 East ramp to I-71 South will be closed. Motorists should continue on I-264 East, take I-71 North, then follow I-265 North to reconnect with I-71 South. Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Motorists should heed signage, use caution when traveling through the work zone, and plan ahead for travel delays. The highway improvement project is expected to be completed by the Fall of 2027. More details, including project timelines and traffic impacts [links-1.govdelivery.com], will be shared online as work progresses.
